minutes.headline: Open Space Committee tells master-plan panel it has no regulatory power over housing, trails, or infrastructure decisions
minutes.summary: The committee spent most of the meeting drafting line-by-line feedback for the town's master plan steering committee, repeatedly clarifying that as an ad-hoc committee of the planning board it can advocate but not regulate, develop, or fund open space uses like trails, dog parks, or gathering spaces. Members also discussed adding an agriculture representative and whether to seek standalone (non-ad-hoc) status during the upcoming bylaw review, and set October 8th (remote) and November 12th as next meetings.

what_happened.line: The committee said it can only advise, not regulate, the town's master-plan panel on housing, trails, and infrastructure.
The chair said unspent school funds are returning to the town and extra free cash went to the district this year, floating both toward Marshall Park.
The chair cited a prior budget override while explaining school funding, then said he had misspoken, and it was not clarified.
Members agreed to explore adding an agriculture representative and to research standalone committee status ahead of the bylaw review.
Next meetings were set for October 8, held remotely for the chair's surgery, and November 12.

why_it_matters: The committee's line-by-line comments feed directly into the town's master plan, which shapes future zoning and capital requests but carries no funding or regulatory force on its own.
A hoped-for funding path for the Marshall Park project rests on school funds being returned to the town and free cash already allocated this year, neither of which this committee controls.
Whether the committee becomes a standalone body during the upcoming bylaw review would change how open space advocacy is structured in town government.
